RENDER MODE — STRICT BLACK AND WHITE PENCIL STORYBOARD SKETCH. The whole artwork is monochrome graphite + ink wash on warm cream sketchbook paper: loose hand-drawn pencil and marker lines, minimal shading, rough cinematic composition. Pencil tones only — no colour fills anywhere unless the [Visual] block below explicitly calls out a DiggerLid yellow accent. The cream paper is the only off-white. One frame from a 60-second ad storyboard series.

[Context] Delivery opening — high drone shot of the machine arriving. Establishes the moment.
[Visual] Top-down drone aerial shot looking straight down at a flatbed delivery truck driving along a country road. On the back of the flatbed: a brand-new XCMG XE17U compact mini-excavator strapped down on a heavy timber pallet, glossy yellow paintwork pristine, tracks unscuffed, factory sticker still on the cab window. Heavy ratchet tie-down straps criss-crossing across the machine and pallet. The flatbed truck is mid-frame, cab at the top, trailer below, driving from top of frame to bottom. Below the truck: bitumen road with painted centre-line, dust kicked up behind the rear wheels, edge of the road bordered by dry grass verges and scattered eucalypt trees. The truck's long shadow runs alongside it. Drone-perspective field of view with slight wide-angle distortion at the edges. Sense of the machine being delivered, arriving.
[Format] 9:16 vertical, single drone-overhead composition.
[Style] B&W storyboard sketch on cream paper, hyperreal sketch detail on the machine, pallet, and tie-down straps, aerial documentary mood. No colour, no text.

[Context] Reveal beat — CAMERA RAMP-UP onto a STATIONARY machine, no cover on it, with a price-tag overlay. The machine itself is not moving; the camera is doing all the work. Conveys: this is a $45K piece of kit, no protection.
[Visual] A STATIONARY XCMG XE17U compact mini-excavator parked dead-still on a clean blank studio backdrop. Tracks square, boom and bucket lowered, motionless — the machine is parked, not moving, not posed mid-action. NO COVER on the cab — operator cab fully exposed, every panel and joystick visible.

The shot is a CAMERA RAMP-UP — the camera is sweeping in low and ramping up toward the machine. Visual cues for the CAMERA motion (not the machine): a dynamic low three-quarter hero angle that suggests the camera tilting upward, a slight wide-angle lens stretch at the edges of the frame, anamorphic horizontal light streaks slicing across the upper third indicating fast camera travel, a faint lens-flare hint at upper-right, soft motion-blur on the very-foreground floor plane suggesting the camera dollying forward. The MACHINE STAYS PIN-SHARP and stationary — no motion lines on the machine itself, no kicked-up dust around the tracks, no leaning into action. The dynamism is camera, not subject.

Layered over the upper-right negative space of the frame, integrated as a clean editorial overlay: a bold black sans-serif typographic price tag reading EXACTLY the seven characters: dollar sign, four, five, comma, zero, zero, zero — i.e. the string '$45,000'. The text is rendered as crisp clean black sans-serif letters, large and confident, NOT touching the machine. Around the text, three small motion-arc accent marks framing it like a callout. The text is the ONLY legible mark in the frame.
[Format] 9:16 vertical, single composition with one clean typographic overlay.
[Style] B&W storyboard sketch on cream paper, kinetic CAMERA-driven energy with a stationary subject, anamorphic feel, editorial hero angle. The '$45,000' overlay must render cleanly with no typos, no missing characters, no extra digits. No other text anywhere.

Persistent characters: Luke and Joel — the two DiggerLid founders, two real Australian tradesmen. Preserve their faces exactly from the reference portraits attached. LUKE = broad-shouldered build, neatly-trimmed dark moustache, ALWAYS wears a black baseball cap with the brim facing forward, dark hair just visible at the temples below the cap line. JOEL = slimmer build, distinctive thick full chevron moustache, mid-brown hair worn in a clean side part, NO cap, clean-shaven on the cheeks and chin.

[Context] The bush workaround — two men mid-fight to cover the machine in pouring rain. Comically inadequate effort.
[Visual] Worksite floor in heavy rain. Diagonal rain streaks slashing across the entire frame. Wet ground. Luke (cap, dark moustache) on the LEFT side of the XE17U excavator, Joel (chevron moustache, no cap) on the RIGHT side. They are mid-action wrangling a sagging olive-green canvas tarp UP and OVER the operator cab — the tarp wrinkled, soaking, slipping off one corner, clearly never designed for this purpose. Luke holding one corner of the wet tarp up over his head, his other hand reaching down with a black rubber ocky strap, hook just about to clip onto the chassis. Joel has a second ocky strap stretched taut across the boom, mid-clip. Both wearing hi-vis raincoats, hoods up — Luke's cap visible under his hood, brim still forward. Faces grimacing, drenched. Bush-fix energy.
[Format] 9:16 vertical, single composition.
[Style] B&W storyboard sketch on cream paper, dramatic rain atmosphere, action-mid-moment energy, hyperreal sketch detail on the wet wrinkled tarp. No colour, no text.

[Context] The workaround fails — moments later. The tarp blows off in a gust. Punchline beat.

CAUGHT MID-ACTION at the instant of failure: the olive-green canvas tarp is mid-air, lifted by a strong gust of wind, twisted and partly folded, motion-blurred and EXITING TOWARD THE UPPER-RIGHT of the frame in one continuous arc. Both black rubber ocky straps SNAPPED — broken ends ricochet outward with motion lines and visible snap-back arcs. Luke (cap, dark moustache) on the LEFT, jumping/reaching upward in vain trying to grab the disappearing tarp, hand outstretched mid-air. Joel (chevron moustache, no cap) on the RIGHT, ducking out of the way as a snapped ocky strap whips past him. Both wearing hi-vis raincoats with hoods up. Faces showing pure ratshit-this-isn't-working frustration. Rain still pouring, debris in the wind, dust kicked up around the tracks.
[Format] 9:16 vertical, single dynamic-action composition.
[Style] B&W storyboard sketch on cream paper, motion blur on the tarp, kinetic snap-back lines on the broken straps, dramatic rain atmosphere. No colour, no text.

[Context] Challenge experiment part 2 — TWO-EXCAVATOR TUG-OF-WAR. The DiggerLid PRO Enclosure cover is pulled in opposite directions by two compact mini-excavators. Industrial-scale stress test.

[Visual] Worksite dirt floor. TWO XCMG XE17U compact mini-excavators facing AWAY from each other on opposite sides of the frame — LEFT machine facing/tracking to the left edge, RIGHT machine facing/tracking to the right edge. Between them, suspended horizontally and stretched TAUT across the middle of the frame: a single grey DiggerLid PRO Enclosure cover. The cover is hooked at each end to the bucket of one of the excavators — LEFT excavator's bucket clamped onto the cover's left edge, RIGHT excavator's bucket clamped onto the cover's right edge — with chain shackles visible at each connection point. Both machines mid-action, hydraulically pulling outward in opposite directions, tracks dug into the dirt, booms back and bucket-arms leaning AWAY from the cover with the strain. The cover is stretched bowstring-taut between them, fabric tension lines clearly visible across the surface, the centre of the cover bowing slightly under the load. Dust kicked up around each machine's tracks from the strain. Stitching holding fast. No tears, no rips. Cinematic side-on hero composition with both machines in equal frame weight.
